title: API Token Controls
scope: Admin controls, logging and revocation for API credentials on SaaS platforms. Sourced from vendor documentation; not an audit of any tenant.

definitions.conditional: Documented, with plan, policy or endpoint conditions.
definitions.excluded: The named control explicitly does not cover this credential.
definitions.not_supported: Vendor documentation states this credential lacks the control.
definitions.unknown: No source found either way. Not a negative finding.
definitions.not_verified: No source found either way. Not a negative finding.
definitions.not_applicable: Does not apply to this credential.
definitions.limited: Documented for a narrower case only.

providers.name: SAP BTP and S/4HANA Cloud
providers.scope_notes: Covers SAP Business Technology Platform (XSUAA, Cloud Management service, btp CLI), SAP Cloud Identity Services, and SAP S/4HANA Cloud Public Edition. Covers BTP Cloud Foundry/multi-environment subaccounts, Identity Authentication tenants, and S/4HANA Cloud Public Edition communication management; BTP docs cited from SAP's official SAP-docs GitHub source of help.sap.com.

controls.name: Delete binding / service key
controls.what: Deleting the binding or service key makes XSUAA stop accepting its secret/certificate.

controls.name: token-validity / refresh-token-validity
controls.what: Sets access/refresh token lifetime per XSUAA instance.

controls.name: Token Validity (subaccount security settings)
controls.what: Sets default token lifetimes for all instances in a subaccount that don't set their own.
controls.setting: BTP cockpit > Subaccount > Security > Settings > Token Validity; Security Settings API

controls.name: Token revoke endpoint
controls.what: Revokes an issued token, but apps validating offline keep accepting it until expiry.

controls.name: Cloud Management service plan selection
controls.what: The cis plan (central, central-viewer, local, local-viewer) fixes the API scopes in the token.

controls.name: Entitlements (SAP Cloud Management service plans)
controls.what: A cis service instance and key can only be created in a subaccount where the global account admin has entitled a Cloud Management service plan.

controls_unknown: Any IP/network allowlist for XSUAA clients, btp API credentials, IAS API secrets or S/4HANA communication users.

auth_paths.name: SAP Cloud Management service (cis) service key

authentication.summary: A service key on a `cis` instance gives an OAuth client for the Accounts/Entitlements/Provisioning APIs. Default grant is password (a user's credentials plus client); client credentials is available when requested at instance creation.

federation.details: Password grant sends a user's password directly to XSUAA; docs reviewed do not say whether IdP MFA/conditional access applies. Client-credential instances have no user.

ip_restriction.boundary: No IP allowlist for OAuth clients/tokens found in the XSUAA docs reviewed.

lifetime.summary: Key lives until deleted; tokens follow XSUAA validity

renewal.summary: Re-request token with key (and user password for password grant).

administration.summary: Global account admin must entitle a cis plan to the subaccount; the plan (central, central-viewer, local, local-viewer) sets the scopes. `central` can create/delete subaccounts and set entitlements.

sso.details: With the Password grant the user's password plus 2FA passcode is needed; the Client Credentials grant has no user check.

sso.ui: BTP cockpit > global account > Security > Trust Configuration > Establish Trust (custom IdP for platform users; enforce MFA there). Client Credentials grant bypasses this.

usage.ui: Account Explorer header > SAP Audit Log Viewer (global account); filter retrieved records for the service key's client ID
usage.api: GET <url_from_service_key>/auditlog/v2/auditlogrecords?time_from=...&time_to=... (Auditlog Management, Central plan); filter on clientId
